html:
SMTO-EXE-0232 — SMTO needs saved registry sign-in details for this image

GUID: 9d1f61f4-68fd-5a3e-9bc0-865edca209ee
Slug: docker-registry-auth-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • To upload (push) or download this Docker image, SMTO needs saved sign-in details for the registry, the online store the image lives in. No registry details were given, or they belong to a different registry. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options (the three dots) and select Parameter Store. Pick Docker registry in the template list, select New, enter the registry address, your username and an access token, then save. SMTO keeps registry sign-ins only in the Parameter Store, so they never appear in the conversation.
  2. Make sure the image name starts with that same registry address and a slash, for example registry.example.com/team/app:1.0. SMTO only sends your sign-in to the registry named at the start of the image.
  3. Ask SMTO again, and type @ in your message to pick the registry parameter you saved. SMTO uses saved sign-in details only when you mention them in the request.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the upload or download finished for that image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the registry account. Never paste your password or token into the conversation; keep it in the Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A registry transfer had no docker_registry Parameter when one is required (always for push), the supplied profile was malformed, or the profile's registry is not the image reference's explicit registry prefix.

What this means

  • Registry credentials were absent when required, invalid as a private registry profile or not bound to the image's explicit registry prefix. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Registry credentials were absent when required, invalid as a private registry profile or not bound to the image's explicit registry prefix.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the public accepted registry reference and image registry identity without exposing its token.

How to fix it

  • Create a Docker registry Parameter (profile_type docker_registry with registry, username and token) in the Parameter Store and pass it as registry_ref by mentioning it in the request. The image reference must begin with that exact registry value followed by a slash (including any port); push always requires it.
  • Select an existing accepted private Docker Parameter reference of the required profile type.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select an existing accepted private Docker Parameter reference of the required profile type.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted profile matches the explicit registry and is delivered only through private transport.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
